accused_victim_relationship: Relative (cousin of the victim's husband); alleged property-related dispute; the appellant had filed a suit claiming the estate of the victim's co-accused relative, as noted by the court
evidence_type: Circumstantial: last-seen testimony of two witnesses; DNA identification report; extra-judicial confession; recovery of scooty on disclosure
confession: Extra-judicial confession to PW-12 (brother-in-law of the victim's father); not relied on, held untenable
trial_court_outcome: Convicted of murder (IPC s.302) by Additional Sessions Judge, Karnal; sentence not stated
neutral_facts: In the early morning of 4 January 2004, a fire was reported in a conical storage structure for cow dung cakes located in an open field in a village. Police found a partly burnt human body in the structure, and a post-mortem recorded it as a female body. Flesh and bone samples were sent for expert opinion. DNA testing of bones and tissue matched the blood samples of the victim's parents, establishing the identity of the deceased. The FIR was lodged in June 2004, after the DNA report. One witness, a relative of the victim's family, stated he saw the accused walking with the victim and her two young children toward a village on the afternoon of 3 January 2004, and later that night saw the accused riding a scooty with a gunny bag on its footrest. Another witness stated he saw the victim with her two children at the accused's house at about 5 pm on 3 January 2004. Both witnesses were shown to have a dispute with the accused over an estate claim. The victim's children were later found at a welfare organisation. An extra-judicial confession was allegedly made to a relative of the victim's family. Police recovered the scooty on the basis of a statement by the accused. The victim's cause of death and the place of death were not established.
physical_harm: Death of the victim; body partly burnt in a storage structure; cause and place of death not established
premeditation_planning: Not found. The court recorded the prosecution's planned-visit story but did not accept that the offence was proved to be premeditated
motive: Not identified (alleged: the accused feared the victim's father would give his property to the victim; court found the primary motive not made out)
key_evidence_accepted: DNA report establishing the death and identity of the deceased; at best, a last-seen inference, which the court held insufficient alone
witness_credibility: Court found the two last-seen witnesses inimical to the accused (estate suit), and found the height discrepancy and the implausibility of carrying a body on a scooty undermined the first witness; statements not reliable without corroboration
post_offence_conduct: Disclosure statement leading to recovery of a scooty; no blood mark or other evidence that it was used in disposing of the body
bail_history: Not stated for earlier stages; bail bonds discharged on acquittal
trial_duration: offence: 3/4 January 2004; trial judgment: 13 January 2006; High Court: 25 March 2008; Supreme Court: 30 July 2019
legal_representation: Appellant: Shaurya Sahay, Amit Kumar, Advocates. State of Haryana: Raj Singh Rana, Pankaj Kumar Singh, Sanjeet Paliwal, Avisek Minj, Vishwa Pal Singh, Advocates
investigation_status: Investigation completed; FIR lodged 15 June 2004 after DNA identification; accused tried
procedural_irregularity: No missing report lodged; FIR lodged about five months after the incident; court held the High Court erred in applying s.106 of the Evidence Act
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted (13.01.2006), sentence not stated. High Court: appeal dismissed (25.03.2008). Supreme Court: appeal allowed; accused acquitted (30.07.2019)
defence_argument: Prosecution story unbelievable and contradictory; last-seen witnesses inimical due to the estate suit; height discrepancy; impossible to ride a scooty with a body on the footrest; PW-5's statement not corroborated; Satpal ruling applies
legal_principle_applied: Section 106 Evidence Act explanation arises only after the prosecution discharges its initial onus; last-seen evidence is weak alone and needs corroboration; chain of circumstances must be complete
precedent_relied_upon: Satpal v. State of Haryana (2018) 6 SCC 610; Asar Mohammad v. State of U.P. 2018 SCC OnLine SC 2179 (which applied Padala Veera Reddy v. State of A.P. 1989 Supp (2) SCC 706 and Mulakh Raj v. Satish Kumar (1992) 3 SCC 43)
other_sentence_order: Bail bonds discharged; accused to be set at liberty if not wanted in any other case
